remarks.name: Thibault Sottiaux
remarks.role: Codex & ChatGPT OpenAI
remarks.text:
Hi Astra users. A reset and a quick update on quality issues that have been posted around.

Working with some of you, we have found and fixed the following issues:
- Some skills written for previous models were triggering too often or preventing the model from checking its work.
- An opt-in context management experiment that could cause early stops or replies to older messages. We've disabled it. Our rough estimate is that 4-5k users were affected by this experiment.
- We've also removed some badly configured engines that resulted in a measured quality degradation for a long tail of traffic flowing through them.

We’ve also made some more minor improvements and things should feel significantly better across the board. More consistent follow-through, better tracking of your latest message, and better checks on the work as it’s going through the motions.

The examples posted and all the users who worked directly with us were incredibly useful in helping fix things quickly. Always grateful for this incredible community.

And of course, a reset is also landing by midnight today.
remarks.translation: Astra 用户们好。这是一次重置，也是对近期大家反馈的质量问题的一次快速更新。在与部分用户合作排查后，我们发现并修复了以下问题： - 一些为旧模型编写的技能触发过于频繁，或妨碍了模型检查自身工作。 - 一项可选加入的上下文管理实验可能导致提前停止或回复到较早的消息。我们已将其禁用。我们粗略估计约有 4-5k 用户受到该实验影响。 - 我们还移除了一些配置不当的引擎，这些引擎导致流经它们的长尾流量出现了可测量的质量下降。 我们还做了一些较小的改进，整体体验应该会明显变好。后续执行更一致，对最新消息的跟踪更好，在工作过程中对成果的检查也更到位。 大家发布的示例以及所有直接与我们合作排查的用户，对快速修复问题起到了极大的帮助。始终感激这个了不起的社区。当然，一次重置也将在今天午夜前落地。
remarks.observation: 这条言论适合观察模型运行、算力、存储、sandbox 或开发平台基础设施的变化；后续事实判断需回到原始公告或技术文档。

remarks.name: Peter Yang
remarks.role: Practical AI tutorials and interviews for busy people
remarks.text:
I am skeptical of "software factories."

Other than for verification & testing, I don't think AI is at a point where it can self-improve a product or build a new feature end-to-end without human in the loop.

Whenever I loop something overnight to build something new = if it makes one wrong assumption the whole thing becomes a waste of tokens. 

What products or features have been built end-to-end with a software factory and no human defining the requirements or checking the work?
remarks.translation: 我对“软件工厂”持怀疑态度。除了用于验证和测试之外，我不认为AI已经到了能够在没有人类参与的情况下自我改进产品或端到端构建新功能的地步。每当我把某件事放到一夜之间循环来构建新东西时＝只要它做出一个错误假设，整件事就变成了对token的浪费。有哪些产品或功能是在没有人类定义需求或检查工作的情况下，通过软件工厂端到端构建出来的？
remarks.observation: 这条言论适合观察 AI 编程工具、设计到代码流程和软件生产方式的变化；需要结合产品发布或文档再做事实判断。

remarks.name: Nikunj Kothari
remarks.role: partner fpvventures - investing in seed/A. previous: early hire meter, opendoor, atlassian & others. love shimoleejhaveri + 👦👧
remarks.text:
“Success has many fathers, but failure is an orphan.”

I never realized the gravity of this quote till I saw extremely successful VCs fight for attribution of the hot deals. 

And you realize this viscerally because the large exits (or markups) are genuinely rare and those are the ones you raise the next fund on (your own or part of the firm). 

This is why in the next couple of years you’ll see many names scrubbed (or conveniently omitted) and everyone wanting to revise history to claim some credit for the ones that eventually succeed. 

So many emerging GPs are facing this explicitly as the only thing they can take to their future LPs is their track record. And it’s been sad to see them not get the credit they actually deserve. 

As @AnjneyMidha said, eventually the new guard will shine as they will figure a way out. But in the short term, hold your founders close since they’ll be the real reference checks! 

(this is genuinely NOT a subtweet at any firm, just what I have been noticing across the market as I’m helping emerging managers)
remarks.translation: “成功有千般父，失败却成孤儿。”直到我亲眼看到极为成功的风投人为争夺热门交易的功劳而争斗时，才真正体会到这句话的分量。你会切身感受到这一点，因为大型退出（或估值跃升）确实罕见，而这些正是你募集下一期基金（无论是你自己的还是所属机构的）所依赖的。这就是为什么未来几年你会看到许多名字被抹去（或被巧妙地省略），人人都想改写历史，为最终成功的项目争一份功劳。许多新兴普通合伙人正明确面临这种处境，因为他们能带给未来有限合伙人的唯一东西就是自己的业绩记录。看到他们得不到本应属于他们的认可，实在令人难过。正如 @AnjneyMidha 所说，最终新一批人终将崭露头角，因为他们会找到出路。但短期内，请紧紧依靠你的创始人，因为他们才是真正的背景调查来源！（这真的不是针对任何机构的暗讽，只是我在帮助新兴管理人时在整个市场中观察到的现象）

remarks.name: Madhu Guru
remarks.role: Sr Director, AI at Meta; Prev: Google - Led Gemini, Veo, Nano Banana.
remarks.text:
Why most enterprise AI efforts fail.

1/ Using old-school playbooks for AI
The CEO picks a trusted lieutenant to lead a central AI team. That leader pulls in a group of trusted people from across the company.

The problem here is the skill gap.

The team structure, product patterns, how you launch and learn that got you here do not work with AI. Much of product development over the last 15 yrs has been incremental improvements.

AI requires experimentation and invention.

2/ Under-investing in evals

Most enterprises don't quite understand the importance of this and what good looks like here. (I have a whole evals series in the comments - check it out)

3/ Building AI for the company from the outside

The central AI team declares itself a platform team and builds tools that everyone is supposed to adopt.

These products are often disconnected from the actual workflows, context and judgment of the people doing the work.

Begrudging adoption follows. But not meaningful productivity gains.

What you should do:

1/ Hire leaders who have done successfully built AI products. You need technical/product depth plus the ability to earn trust with the people whose jobs they’re helping reinvent.

2/ Make evals a first class citizen in your AI efforts

3/ Embed your best AI builders inside the functions you want to transform. Build * with * finance , build * with * sales, build * with * support.
remarks.translation: 为什么大多数企业AI努力会失败。1/ 用老一套方法来搞AI CEO挑选一位信任的副手来领导一个中央AI团队。这位负责人从全公司拉来一群信任的人。问题在于技能差距。让你走到今天的团队结构、产品模式、发布和学习方式，在AI上行不通。过去15年里，产品开发大多是渐进式改进。AI需要的是实验和发明。2/ 对评估投入不足 大多数企业不太理解这一点的重要性，也不清楚好的评估是什么样子。（我在评论区有一个完整的评估系列——可以去看看）3/ 从外部为公司构建AI 中央AI团队自称是平台团队，构建所有人都应该采用的工具。这些产品往往与实际工作流程、具体情境以及实际做事的人的判断脱节。随之而来的是勉强采用。但并没有带来有意义的生产力提升。你应该做的是：1/ 聘请有过成功构建AI产品经验的领导者。你需要技术/产品深度，以及赢得那些工作正被帮助重塑的人信任的能力。2/ 让评估成为你AI工作中的一等公民。3/ 把你最好的AI构建者嵌入到你想转型的职能部门中。与财务一起构建，与销售一起构建，与支持一起构建。

podcasts.originalExcerpt: A few years ago, Caltech Prof. and co-founder of Accelerated Understanding, Anima Anandkumar set out to develop the first open-source weather model with AI. Talking to experts in the field, she was met with skepticism. Weather is chaotic, physics simulations are hard, have been developed for decades, and require supercomputers, the data just isn’t there. Despite reservations, Anima went forth and built. Within a year her team had developed FourCastNet, a predictive model that is competitive with the best physics-based simulations available. Thanks to Anima, and her follow up work, anyone can now predict weather accurately over a short timescale using consumer grade GPUs.
